title: Organize the Expedition
content:
What problem does this solve?
Several related values are easier to manage as one collection than as many separate variable names. A list stores values in a specific order.

Start with the behavior
  items = ["a", "b", "c"]
  print(items[0])
The list keeps three values in order. Python numbers their positions starting at 0, so [0] means the first item.

Keep count and position separate
A three-item list has three items, but its valid indexes are 0, 1, and 2. The last index is one less than the number of items.

Vocabulary after the behavior
The list is an ordered collection. The number inside square brackets is an index. Python's list indexes are zero-based.
concepts: A list stores several values in order
A three-item list has valid indexes 0, 1, and 2
Square brackets retrieve the value at one position

examples.title: Three values
examples.explanation: Indexes 0 and 2 retrieve the first and third values.

examples.title: Expedition roster
examples.explanation: The roster is one ordered value rather than four unrelated variables.

common_mistakes: Expecting the first item to be index 1
Using an index equal to the number of items
Confusing the list itself with one value inside the list

exercises.title: First index
hints: items[0] means the first value in the list.

exercises.title: Read the second item
exercises.prompt: Change the index so the program prints exactly blue.
hints: The first item is index 0, so the second item is the next index.

tests.message: Retrieve a list item with an index.

exercises.title: Read the third item
exercises.prompt: The names list is supplied. Print Sam by indexing the list. Do not print the literal string "Sam" directly.
exercises.starter_code:
names = ["Ada", "Lin", "Sam"]

# Print the third item by indexing names
hints: There are three items, but their indexes are 0, 1, and 2.
Sam is the third item, so use index 2.

tests.message: Use list indexing rather than printing the literal name.

exercises.title: Two lookups
exercises.prompt: What are the two output lines?
hints: Map each index to its position before thinking about output order.
The output is 30 on the first line and 20 on the second.

exercises.title: Off by one
exercises.prompt: The program intends to print c but raises an error. Repair only the index.
hints: Count how many items are present, then list their valid indexes.
Three items means the valid indexes are 0, 1, and 2.

exercises.title: Roster card
exercises.prompt:
Create exactly this list:
party = ["Aria", "Rook", "Mira", "Selene"]

Then print exactly:
Leader: Aria
Scout: Mira

Retrieve both names by indexing party inside f-strings.
exercises.starter_code: # Create party, then build the two roster lines
hints: First create the four-item party list in the required order.
Aria is index 0 and Mira is index 2. Put those lookups inside f-strings.
exercises.success_message: You used positions in one collection to build two readable roster fields.
